method.engine: ASE 3 + mace-torch (cuEquivariance, float32) on NVIDIA GB10
method.protocol: Solid-liquid coexistence (interface direction) method. 4x4x8 fcc supercell (512 atoms) from MACE-relaxed a0=4.039 A; solid equilibrated by anisotropic Berendsen NPT at 900 K (1.5 ps); top half melted with Langevin at 2250 K (2 ps) while bottom half fixed, then 0.5 ps at 900 K; coexistence runs at 825/900/975/1050 K with anisotropic Berendsen NPT (P=0, taut=100 fs, taup=500 fs), 7 ps each. Phase growth judged from potential-energy drift (fit t>1 ps) and final fraction of 12-coordinated atoms. Results: 825 K slope -0.0094 eV/atom/ps, CN12 fraction 0.65 (crystal grows); 900 K +0.0026, 0.19 (melts); 975 K +0.0086, 0.04 (melts); 1050 K +0.0070, 0.04 (melts). Tm bracketed in (825, 900) K; reported value = bracket midpoint, uncertainty = half-width.

results.note: PREMISE: Tm is well-defined and accessible with an MLIP by two-phase coexistence (avoids the superheating of single-phase heating); 512 atoms and 7 ps are enough to see the interface move at |T-Tm| >~ 40 K but not to resolve Tm more finely. VALIDATION (same model, cell shape, protocol, run length): Cu, independent ITS-90 fixed point 1357.77 K (tier1.json, NIST): crystal grew at 1200 and 1300 K, melted at 1400 and 1500 K -> MACE-MP-0 Tm(Cu) in (1300,1400) K, consistent with experiment. RESULT: MACE-MP-0 Tm(Al) in (825, 900) K; linear interpolation of the energy-drift zero gives ~884 K, inside the bracket. The measured Al melting point is 933.45 K (NIST-JANAF, tier1.json), i.e. this model predicts a melting point roughly 35-110 K too low (~4-12%); the experimental value lies outside the simulated bracket, so the discrepancy is attributed to the potential (PBE-trained foundation model, not fit to Al liquid thermodynamics), not to sampling. For the physical answer use 933.45 K; this number is the MACE-MP-0 prediction. UNCERTAINTY (+/-38 K) covers only the temperature-grid bracketing resolution; it does NOT cover the model (DFT/MLIP) error, finite-size effects (512 atoms, ~16 A interfaces separation), Berendsen barostat artefacts, float32 precision, or stochastic interface fluctuations (one run per T). The 900 K run had only a small positive drift, so Tm(MACE) is probably in the upper part of the bracket (~870-895 K).

payload.note: I tried to prove the result wrong and could not. (1) Premise: well posed. Al is an elemental fcc metal with a sharp, congruent first-order melting transition at ambient pressure. Pressure dependence is about 7 K/GPa, so the 1 bar vs 1 atm difference is ~1e-5 K. (2) Anchor: I fetched the live NIST-JANAF Al-001 table myself. It lists '933.450 ... 17.982 CRYSTAL <--> LIQUID' and '933.450 ... 28.693 TRANSITION', which matches the reported 933.45 K and the tier1.json record exactly. The ITS-90 Al freezing-point fixed point, 933.473 K, agrees within 0.023 K, inside the stated +/-0.1 K. tier1.json gives that alternate only from an unofficial copy, but it fits the well-known 660.323 C fixed point. (3) Consistency: the JANAF enthalpy jump (10.711 kJ/mol, about 397 kJ/kg) is consistent with the same record. No contradiction. (4) Method: the reported number is a measured reference value, not a simulation result. That is appropriate because the task asks for the melting point of Al, not a model prediction, and the worker states this transparently. The earlier MACE-MP-0 coexistence estimate (bracket 825-900 K, 512 atoms, one seed per T, 7 ps) is correctly demoted to a failed cross-check, consistent with my previous 'disagree' (b0465de9). The worker's claim that PBE-level models tend to underestimate Tm(Al) is a soft literature generalization that I did not verify, and it does not affect the reported value. Minor: the method.engine and model fields mix the reference value with the cross-check, which makes the board summary hard to read but does not change the answer. Verdict: pass. Tm(Al, ambient pressure) = 933.45 +/- 0.1 K.
